What is the equation of the ellipse given above?
after.worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=3$ and the vertical radius has length $b=1.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

a
x21+y23=1
b
x23+y21=1
c
x26+y21=1
d
x29+y21=1

x21+y29=1

EXPLANATION

Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length a and a vertical radius of length b is given by x2a2+y2b2=1.

Here, the horizontal radius has length a=3 and the vertical radius has length b=1. Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is x2a2+y2b2=1x232+y212=1x29+y21=1.

Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=3$ and the vertical radius has length $b=1.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{1} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

after.worked_solution:
Remember that the equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the horizontal radius has length $a=3$ and the vertical radius has length $b=8.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{8}^{2}} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{64} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
